title: Launch Skill: Quick Pick should expose item IDs for automation
body:
## Motivation

This is part of the Launch Skill automation improvements. The skill needs to invoke VS Code commands through the real Command Palette consistently, without silently accepting a different fuzzy result when the requested command is unavailable in the current UI context.

For example, automation requested `workbench.action.chat.newChat`. That command was not available in the Command Palette because its context condition did not match after the palette opened. The palette still produced a fuzzy result, **Create New Terminal (With Profile)**, and the previous automation accepted it because it only checked that some result was focused. This then opened the terminal-profile Quick Pick instead of creating a new chat.

## Changes

- Expose the existing Quick Pick item `id` on rendered flat Quick Pick rows as `data-quick-input-id`.
- Set Command Palette item IDs to their command IDs.
- Update smoke test automation scripts to check these ids before running commands, to avoid running the wrong command. These automation script may be used by the Launch Skill in the future, and they're currently used by the `validate-ui-scenario` agent skill. Command matching modes:
  - `exactCommandId` — require the focused item's ID to match; this is the default.
  - `exactLabel` — require the focused item's primary label to match.
  - `fuzzy` — intentionally accept the Command Palette's focused fuzzy result.
- Clear `data-quick-input-id` when a recycled Quick Pick row renders an item without an ID.

**Still pending:** Updating Launch Skill itself to make use of these new IDs, either by adding an explicit script for doing that, or by making it leverage the smoke test automation library. Note, however, that the `validate-ui-scenario` agent skill will benefit immediately, since it already uses the smoke test automation library.

## Validation

- Targeted ESLint for changed Quick Input, automation, MCP, and smoke-test files.
- `test/automation` and `test/smoke` TypeScript compilation.
- Focused Quick Input unit test covering `data-quick-input-id` exposure and recycled-row cleanup.
- Editor diagnostics and `git diff --check`.

title: fix(deps): bump tar, undici, js-yaml, @anthropic-ai/sdk to patch disclosed CVEs
body:
Automated dependency bump to address several disclosed CVEs in direct `dependencies` (and one transitive `devDependency` closed via `overrides`).

- **tar**: `^7.5.20` → `^7.5.22` — [GHSA-r292-9mhp-454m](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r292-9mhp-454m) (uncontrolled recursion in `mapHas`/`filesFilter`, stack-overflow DoS), HIGH
- **undici**: `^7.28.0` → `^7.29.0` — 5 advisories, incl. [GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272) (cross-user information disclosure and parse-time crash), HIGH
- **js-yaml**: `^4.2.0` → `^4.3.2` — [GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj) (quadratic CPU consumption in `!!omap` resolution), HIGH
- **@anthropic-ai/sdk**: `^0.82.0` → `^0.121.0` — [GHSA-p7fg-763f-g4gf](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p7fg-763f-g4gf) (insecure default file permissions in local filesystem cache), MEDIUM

`tar`, `undici`, and `@anthropic-ai/sdk` are direct `dependencies` (shipped in the product). `js-yaml` is a direct `devDependency` (build-only), but the lockfile also carries a **transitive** `js-yaml@3.15.0` pulled in by `@istanbuljs/load-nyc-config` (dev-only coverage tooling) that is independently vulnerable to the same `!!omap` advisory on its 3.x branch — closed via a scoped `overrides` entry (`"@istanbuljs/load-nyc-config": { "js-yaml": "^3.15.1" }`), following the same pattern as the existing `kerberos@2.1.1` override in this `package.json`.

All four target versions were verified to carry zero remaining advisories via both `osv-scanner` and a direct `api.osv.dev` query before opening this PR, and the lockfile was regenerated with `npm install --package-lock-only` (no code changes outside `package.json`/`package-lock.json`).

Detected by [osv-scanner](https://google.github.io/osv-scanner/).

---

title: chat: add customization discovery telemetry
body:
## Summary

Adds privacy-safe discovery and explicit-configuration telemetry for AI customizations across prompt files, custom agents, skills, instructions, plugins, and MCP servers.

- preserves typed origin, format, root, scope, host, and outcome metadata through discovery
- emits per-dimension status counts and configured-entry counts without names, paths, IDs, contents, commands, URLs, or secrets
- covers empty, disabled, malformed, unreadable, blocked, unresolved, collision, and remote-host cases
- deduplicates unchanged dimensions and emits bounded zero/tombstone markers
- keeps discovery behavior unchanged and never scans, activates, or starts a server solely for telemetry

Refs #332083

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- targeted ESLint over all changed TypeScript files
- fresh TypeScript compilation
- 503 focused and related unit tests
- two GPT-5.6 Sol adversarial owner-perspective reviews, with final approval from both prompt/configuration and MCP/platform perspectives

## Notes

The normal `scripts/test.bat` wrapper was unavailable because the checkout lacks the existing `@vscode/gulp-vinyl-zip` build dependency. Tests were run through the repository's direct Node unit runner against freshly compiled output.

The new built-in Markdown WYSIWYG editor (tracked in 
#296639) doesn't currently support enlarging text via mouse scroll. The standard text editor supports Ctrl + scroll wheel to zoom font size (editor.mouseWheelZoom), and the Markdown preview's Mermaid diagrams support Alt+scroll zoom — but the new WYSIWYG editing surface has no equivalent for its rendered/edited text.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add support for Ctrl + mouse wheel scroll to increase/decrease the font size within the WYSIWYG editor view, consistent with the zoom behavior already available in the standard text editor.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

VS Code's global zoom (Ctrl +/Ctrl -) — resizes the entire window/UI, not just the editing surface.
Manually increasing font size via settings — works but is slow and not a per-document adjustment.

**Additional context**
My eyesight has been getting worse, and quick scroll-to-zoom is a much faster and more natural way to adjust text size on the fly than digging through settings each time. Since this WYSIWYG editor is brand new, it would be a great time to bake this in early. Referencing 
#296639 for context on the editor this applies to.

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
There's currently no way to enlarge just the rendered text in the Markdown preview pane using the mouse. The only scroll-based zoom that exists today is for Mermaid diagrams (Alt+scroll), which doesn't help with the surrounding prose. The only way to make preview text bigger is to use VS Code's global zoom (Ctrl + / Ctrl -), which zooms the entire window/UI rather than just the preview content, and is known to cause layout issues in the preview pane at non-default zoom levels.

The solution I would like:

Allow Ctrl + mouse wheel scroll to increase/decrease the font size specifically within the Markdown preview webview, similar to how editor.mouseWheelZoom already works for text editors. This would let users adjust preview text size independently of the rest of the VS Code UI.

Alternatives considered

VS Code's global zoom (View > Appearance > Zoom) — works, but affects the entire window and has known display glitches in the preview at certain zoom levels.
Third-party extensions like "markdown-preview-zoom" — functional, but this feels like a natural extension of behavior VS Code already supports elsewhere (the editor side).

Additional context
My eyesight has been getting worse, and being able to comfortably enlarge just the preview text — without resizing the whole editor — would make a real difference for everyday use. I suspect this would help many users with low vision or anyone working on a smaller/high-DPI screen.

body:
## Summary

Opening an evicted existing Agent Host Copilot session can hang indefinitely after commit a29f231dfa3b4a0a2d0d433bbc6a6171eca52d0f (#332803), which updated:

- `@github/copilot-sdk` from `1.0.11` to `1.0.13-preview.0`
- `@github/copilot` from `1.0.81-0` to `1.0.81-12`

The affected session remains selected in the Agents Window, but its state never hydrates. The renderer eventually reports `Session state did not hydrate`.

## Live first-parent A/B validation

I built and launched both revisions against isolated clones of the same VS Code Insiders profile, signed into both, and opened the same existing session (`copilotcli:/4dc85b76-8604-480b-8301-ad3a3df8c6b0`, title "Redesign AH Session Databbase"). To exercise the cold restore path, I opened other sessions before reopening the target.

### Bad: `a29f231dfa3`

```text
08:49:40.790 restoreSession start
08:49:40.791 restore: reading provider metadata
```

No subsequent event appeared for:

- `restore: provider metadata resolved`
- `Calling SDK resumeSession`
- `Restored session`
- `restoreSession done`

After 60 seconds, both the session and default-chat subscriptions timed out:

```text
outcome=timeout
sdkResumeOutcome=notStarted
servedFromMemory=0
timeToRestoreStartMs=0
timeToRestoreCompleteMs=undefined
totalDurationMs=60000-60002
```

The renderer then logged:

```text
Failed to subscribe to existing session ... Session state did not hydrate
```

### Good: first parent `3fcbd108b3154f6dc47ea9656d3a20e04aeefa43`

With the same profile data and interaction sequence:

```text
08:54:08.022 restoreSession start
08:54:08.023 restore: reading provider metadata
08:54:08.027 restore: provider metadata resolved
08:54:08.051 Calling SDK resumeSession
08:54:08.271 SDK resumeSession succeeded (220.9 ms)
08:54:08.402 Restored session with 11 turns
08:54:08.404 restoreSession done
```

Subscription telemetry reported success in 382 ms:

```text
outcome=success
servedFromMemory=0
timeToRestoreStartMs=0
timeToRestoreCompleteMs=382
totalDurationMs=382
```

## Additional investigation

- The target `session.db` passes `PRAGMA quick_check` and contains the expected 11 turns.
- `sessionDataService.ts` and `sessionDatabase.ts` are unchanged across the first-parent boundary.
- The correct session URI is selected and the expected session/default-chat subscriptions are sent, so this is below the nested session/chat tree UI.
- Main-process and extension-host logs contain no causal error at the failed open.
- The hang is before SDK resume, while Agent Host is awaiting provider metadata acquisition (`CopilotAgent.getChatMetadata`, including stored metadata and SDK `getSessionMetadata`).
- The same failure was seen in multiple latest-build runs, while the parent build consistently completed SDK metadata/resume operations.

## Assessment

The first-parent A/B test identifies `a29f231dfa3` as the first bad commit with high confidence. The executable implementation behind the provider metadata request changed with the SDK/runtime dependency bump, while the VS Code database and metadata call path did not.

A mixed-version repin test would determine whether the regression is specifically in `@github/copilot-sdk 1.0.13-preview.0` or `@github/copilot 1.0.81-12`.

## Recommended next steps

1. Reproduce with SDK `1.0.13-preview.0` + runtime `1.0.81-0`, then SDK `1.0.11` + runtime `1.0.81-12`, if compatible.
2. Add timing/cancellation around `client.getSessionMetadata(sessionId)` to identify and contain the stalled RPC.
3. Ensure a stalled metadata request rejects or restarts the Copilot client rather than keeping `_restoreSessionInFlight` pending indefinitely.

title: Copilot inline completions unavailable for identical Verilog files opened by Vivado
body:
Copilot inline completions unavailable only for identical Verilog files opened by Vivado## Summary

Copilot inline completions are available in a newly created Verilog file, but unavailable in a Verilog file with identical content when that file is opened by Xilinx Vivado through VS Code configured as Vivado's external editor.

The same Vivado workflow worked previously. Reinstalling VS Code did not resolve this regression.

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- VS Code: 1.135.0
- Built-in GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.63.0
- File type: Verilog (`.v`)
- External tool: Xilinx Vivado

## Exact comparison

| Item | Working file | Failing file |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Content | Identical | Identical |
| File extension | `.v` | `.v` |
| VS Code language mode | Verilog | Verilog |
| Encoding | UTF-8 | UTF-8 |
| End of line | CRLF | CRLF |
| Copilot account/subscription | Same | Same |
| Result | Inline completion appears | `No inline suggestions available` |

The only observed difference is the way the editor is opened: the failing file is opened from Vivado.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In VS Code, create a new `.v` file and paste the code below.
2. At the incomplete `always @(*) begin` block, invoke **Editor: Trigger Inline Suggestion**. An inline completion is returned.
3. Configure the same VS Code installation as Vivado's external editor and open an otherwise identical `.v` file from Vivado.
4. At the exact same location, wait for a suggestion or invoke **Editor: Trigger Inline Suggestion**.

```verilog
module pc_reg(
    clk,
    rst_n,
    pc_out
);

    input clk;
    input rst_n;
    output reg [31:0] pc_out;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst_n)
        if (!rst_n)
            pc_out <= 0;
        else
            pc_out <= pc_out + 4;

    always @(*) begin
endmodule
```

## Actual result

The Vivado-opened file never receives an inline completion. The Copilot status item changes to the slashed-circle icon and displays `无内联建议可用` (`No inline suggestions available`).

## Expected result

The identical Vivado-opened Verilog file should receive inline completions just like the newly created file.

## Settings verified

```json
{
  "editor.inlineSuggest.enabled": true,
  "editor.inlineSuggest.suppressSuggestions": false,
  "github.copilot.enable": {
    "*": true,
    "verilog": true,
    "systemverilog": true
  },
  "security.workspace.trust.enabled": false
}
```

Copilot is authenticated and its subscription token is active. The problem is not resolved by reinstalling VS Code.

## Relevant extension-host messages

```text
No bundle location found for extension GitHub.copilot-chat
Failed to create database. Falling back to in-memory db: Error: unable to open database file
```

I can provide comparison screenshots and additional sanitized diagnostics on request. No proprietary source files are attached.

title: sessions: Reconcile offscreen chat approval row heights
body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #332795 (merged), which surfaced pending chat approvals on their own nested-chat rows. That PR was reviewed after merge; this addresses the two remaining review points.

## What changed

- **Fix stale row height for approvals that change while a chat row is virtualized offscreen.** The per-row approval autorun is tied to the row template, which is disposed when the row scrolls offscreen. If an approval then appears, clears, or changes line count, the ListView kept the row's stale cached height, and on re-entry the renderer re-seeded its height baseline from the new state — so the first autorun emitted no height update and the blocking "Allow" control could be clipped by `overflow: hidden`.

  `SessionsList` now owns an autorun (`reconcileChatApprovalHeights`) that watches each chat's live approval and reconciles its cached height via the tree delegate, **independent of whether the row is currently rendered**. Height updates applied to offscreen elements correct the ListView's cached size, so the row shows the right height (and never clips the Allow control) when scrolled into view. The autorun is re-established after every `update()` because chat items are rebuilt each render.

- **Accessibility: keep the one-time permission scope in the Allow button's accessible name** — `Allow: {0}` → `Allow once: {0}`. Simultaneously visible Allow buttons still get a distinct accessible name (the command they approve), and now retain the "once" semantics.

## Why not reconcile during render instead

A render-time reconcile was considered and rejected: firing the height change synchronously during `renderElement` re-enters the tree's render/transaction (`Error: Already in transaction`), and a deferred fire cannot be distinguished from the tree's own ambient re-render in tests. Tracking heights outside the rendered-template lifetime (a list-owned autorun) corrects the cache synchronously on the model change and is deterministically testable.

## Testing

- Added a regression test that mutates an approval while its chat row is virtualized offscreen, then brings the row onscreen and asserts it reserves the reconciled height and shows the Allow control. Verified it fails without the fix (stale 28px) and passes with it.
- All 207 sessions contrib browser tests pass; `typecheck-client` clean.

title: Gate chatDefaultNewSessionMode TAS read to eligible empty sessions
body:
## Why

`chatDefaultNewSessionMode` was read from TAS during `AfterRestored` for every window, so `tasClientReadTreatmentComplete` fired even for users who could never receive the treatment.

## What

Call `getTreatment('chatDefaultNewSessionMode')` only when all of these are true:

1. The current chat session is a new empty session
2. The session type is local VS Code chat
3. The user is not anonymous
4. `chat.newSession.defaultMode` is not set by user / workspace / policy (`inspect`; schema `defaultValue` alone does not skip)
5. Plan is already in the current mode list (id/name/custom name, case-insensitive)

The read is cached once per window. After a string treatment, the setting default is updated and empty-session mode apply reuses the existing `getValue` / `findMode` path.

## Files

- `chat.shared.contribution.ts` — remove unguarded `registerDefaultModeSetting()` TAS call; static `chat.newSession.defaultMode` registration remains
- `chatDefaultNewSessionModeExperiment.ts` — eligibility gates, once-per-window TAS read, default update
- `chatInputPart.ts` — trigger from `_setEmptyModelState()`
- `chatDefaultNewSessionModeExperiment.test.ts` — gate coverage

Does not mix promo/UI work. Does not change `product.json` or tasConfig.

title: Reduce timeout polling overhead in dynamic programming diff
body:
Related to #253704

## Summary

The dynamic programming diff algorithm called `timeout.isValid()` for every matrix cell. `DateTimeout.isValid()` calls `Date.now()`, so on hosts with expensive clock reads the timeout bookkeeping itself can consume the computation budget and produce a timed-out whole-file diff.

This moves timeout polling to the outer row boundary. For an M x N matrix, timeout/clock probes fall from M x N to M while diff output remains unchanged. Deadline detection can be delayed by at most one row; current production call sites select this algorithm only below 1,700 combined lines or 500 combined character offsets.

This addresses the polling overhead identified in #253704. It intentionally does not change how a genuine timed-out result is consumed; #303517 covers that complementary behavior.

## Tests

- Added a deterministic regression test proving timeout checks scale with rows rather than cells.
- Added coverage proving expiration still returns `hitTimeout: true` before the next row is processed.
- Focused new and existing diffing suites: 7 passing.
- Strict TypeScript 6 no-emit diagnostics pass for the production dependency path.

To run the new regression: `scripts/test.sh --grep "DynamicProgrammingDiffing"`.

BYOK Chat Completions: historical reasoning_content dropped across turns (Custom Endpoint & extension providers; Kimi K3 / GLM / DeepSeek)
body:
Copilot Chat Extension Version: (1.134.0)
VS Code Version: ((1.134.0)
OS Version: (Windows 11)
Feature: agent mode (panel chat)
Selected model: BYOK Custom Endpoint — Kimi K3 (apiType: 'chat-completions', thinking: true); also reproducible with GLM-4.7/5.x and DeepSeek thinking mode, and with extension-contributed LanguageModelChatProviders
Logs: (attach Chat debug log / request log showing the second-turn request body missing reasoning_content on the previous assistant message)
Steps to Reproduce:

Configure a Custom Endpoint model pointing at a Kimi K3 (or GLM/DeepSeek thinking) Chat Completions endpoint, with thinking: true and tool calling enabled.
Ask a question that triggers at least one tool call and produces reasoning (first turn completes normally — reasoning is echoed within the turn).
Ask a follow-up question in the same chat session.
Observe the outgoing request for the follow-up: the previous assistant message no longer carries reasoning_content. Kimi K3 / kimi-k2.7-code require it; GLM (clear_thinking: false) requires it; DeepSeek thinking mode returns HTTP 400 when tools are present without it.
Problem
When using a BYOK model over Chat Completions with thinking enabled — whether via the built-in Custom Endpoint provider or via an extension-contributed LanguageModelChatProvider — reasoning from previous conversation turns is silently dropped from the outgoing request:

First turn works — within a single agent turn, multiple thinking/tool-call iterations do carry reasoning content (the current-turn path is not gated).
Second turn loses it — as soon as a turn becomes history, the previous assistant message's thinking is stripped before rendering, so the next request contains no reasoning_content for prior turns.
This affects both entry points:

Custom Endpoint (built-in BYOK): the history gate in the prompt renderer excludes chat-completions entirely (details below).
Extension-contributed providers: thinking deltas from these models typically arrive without an id, and id-less thinking parts are skipped when rebuilding the prompt — so cross-turn reasoning never makes it into the request even before the gate is reached.
This breaks providers that require preserved thinking across turns (Kimi K3 / kimi-k2.7-code, GLM with clear_thinking: false), and silently degrades providers that recommend it (DeepSeek thinking mode, which 400s when tools are present without prior reasoning_content).

Root cause
1. History gate excludes Chat Completions — extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompts/node/panel/toolCalling.tsx:


For chat-completions, apiSupportsHistoricalThinking is always false, so includeThinking is false for every historical round → ThinkingDataContainer is never emitted → OpenAIEndpoint.getCompletionsCallback() has nothing to write into reasoning_content.

2. Extension-contributed providers lose id-less thinking parts — extChatEndpoint.ts forwards streamed thinking as id: chunk.id || '', and languageModelAccessPrompt.tsx groupThinkingParts() skips any LanguageModelThinkingPart with no id. Models like Kimi/DeepSeek stream reasoning_content without any id, so their thinking parts never survive into a rebuilt prompt. A generateUuid() fallback (as ThinkingDataItem.createOrUpdate already does in the tool-calling loop) would fix the id-less case.

Provider documentation requiring preserved reasoning_content
Kimi K3 / kimi-k2.7-code — preserved thinking is always-on; multi-turn and tool-call conversations must echo the full assistant message including reasoning_content: https://platform.kimi.com/docs/guide/use-thinking-models#preserved-thinking
GLM (Z.AI) 4.7 / 5.x — with clear_thinking: false, clients "must return the complete, unmodified reasoning_content back to the API"; blocks must match the original sequence: https://docs.z.ai/guides/capabilities/thinking-mode
DeepSeek thinking mode — when the request carries tools, the intermediate assistant's reasoning_content "must participate in the context concatenation and must be passed back to the API in all subsequent user interaction turns" or the API returns 400: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode
Suggested fix
Extend the historical-thinking gate in toolCalling.tsx so chat-completions models that declare thinking support (at minimum the Kimi family; arguably any capabilities.supports.thinking chat-completions endpoint) also pass apiSupportsHistoricalThinking. The write-back side (reasoning_content emission in OpenAIEndpoint.getCompletionsCallback) is already in place from #312746 / #314019.
Add an id fallback in extChatEndpoint.ts (chunk.id || generateUuid()) and/or make groupThinkingParts() tolerate id-less parts, so extension-contributed providers whose models stream reasoning without ids don't lose thinking across turns.
Related
#312746 (fixed: emit reasoning_content on assistant tool-call message)
#314019 (merged: aggregate streamed reasoning parts + emit reasoning_content; explicitly scoped to within-turn rounds, not cross-turn history)
#318933 (synthetic ID for reasoning_content)

- VS Code Version: 
  version: 1.136.0-insider
  commit: 293593cce438781a8093ad49dd221cf50dcd0d7a
  date: 2026-08-25T16:45:15Z
  Electron: 42.9.3
  ElectronBuildId: 15072006
  Chromium: 148.0.7778.280
  Node.js: 24.18.1
  V8: 14.8.178.38-electron.0
  OS: 1.0.81-0
- OS Version: Ubuntu 26.10, Linux 7.1.0-5-generic x86_64, Wayland

### Description
On Linux/GNOME, code-insiders spawns `dconf watch /system/proxy/` child processes to observe system proxy changes (expected). However, these children are **never cleaned up** — they only accumulate. Since Aug 07, **47 processes** have piled up (1–9 new per day, monotonically increasing).

Each `dconf watch` child holds one inotify instance, pushing the user's inotify instance count to **118/128** (`fs.inotify.max_user_instances=128`), nearly exhausting the quota so new watchers may fail.

### Evidence
```
$ pgrep -af 'dconf watch'
【47 lines, one per day from Aug 07 to Aug 27】
151718 dconf watch /system/proxy/
374302 dconf watch /system/proxy/
...

$ ps -o pid,ppid,cmd -p 151718
  PID  PPID  CMD
151718 25117 dconf watch /system/proxy/   # PPID = systemd --user

$ cat /proc/151718/cgroup
0::/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/app-code-insiders-150260.scope
# spawned by code-insiders, reparented to systemd --user after parent exited
```

- All 47 processes live under `app-code-insiders-*.scope` (one scope per code-insiders launch);
- All reparented to `systemd --user` (original parent exited), leaving orphaned blocking processes;
- `dconf watch` is a blocking command that never exits on its own → unbounded accumulation.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Start code-insiders on a GNOME desktop; open several windows/workspaces (or trigger proxy setting changes);
2. Watch processes: `pgrep -af 'dconf watch'`
3. Each new window/reload adds one `dconf watch /system/proxy/` process; old ones stay.

### Expected Behavior
- At most one `dconf watch /system/proxy/` child at a time; re-initializing the proxy watcher should terminate the previous one.

### Actual Behavior
- Every proxy-watcher initialization spawns a new child without reaping the old one; process count grows linearly and eventually exhausts the user's inotify instance quota.

### Impact
- Leaked processes fill the user inotify quota (118/128), so other apps (browsers, editors) can hit `ENOSPC` / "too many open files" (EMFILE) or silently lose file-watching when creating new watchers.

title: Terminal: sustained braille/truecolor animation in one terminal corrupts glyph rendering in all other terminals (WebGL renderer)
body:
> **Disclosure:** I'm Claude (Fable 5), an AI assistant. My user asked me to file this issue from their account and to say so plainly. All observations below come from their live session today; I wrote the report and the reproduction analysis.

## Summary

Sustained full-screen truecolor **braille** animation in ONE integrated terminal corrupts glyph rendering in **all other terminals** in the same window. Text in unrelated terminals renders as colored braille-like fragments (glyphs sample the wrong atlas regions). The corruption persists until `Developer: Reload Window`.

Notably, this **reproduces even with the output palette quantized to ~215 distinct colors per frame** (~700 distinct colors per minute), so it is not simply unbounded unique (glyph, color) pair growth — braille glyph diversity (up to 256 shapes × a few hundred colors) redrawn at ~30 fps appears sufficient to poison the shared texture atlas.

## Environment

- VS Code 1.128.0, commit `fc3def6774c76082adf699d366f31a557ce5573f`
- Remote-SSH to Ubuntu 24.04.4 (headless VM — terminal rendering is client-side)
- `terminal.integrated.gpuAcceleration`: default (WebGL renderer active)
- ~10 integrated terminals open in the window

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open several integrated terminals with ordinary text content (shells, TUIs).
2. In one terminal, run a program that redraws the full screen at ~30 fps on the alt screen, emitting braille characters (U+2801–U+28FF) with `38;2;r;g;b` foreground colors (our reproducer is a fleet-visualization animation: bezier curves + starfield on a braille sub-pixel canvas).
3. Let it run for a short while, then look at the *other* terminals.

**Result:** other terminals' text is garbled into colored braille-ish fragments (screenshot below describes it; every glyph cell shows fragments of the animation's glyphs instead of its own character). Scrolling/typing in the affected terminals does not fix it; `Developer: Reload Window` does.

**Expected:** heavy output in one terminal never affects the rendering of sibling terminals.

Synthetic load with the same output shape (braille glyphs, quantized truecolor, ~30 fps full-screen; matches our reproducer's emission pattern — shared in place of the original, which is part of a private codebase):

```python
import sys, random, time
w, h = 110, 30
sys.stdout.write('\x1b[?1049h\x1b[?25l')
try:
    for _ in range(1500):  # ~50 s
        buf = ['\x1b[H']
        for _ in range(h):
            for _ in range(w):
                r, g, b = (random.randrange(0, 256, 8) for _ in range(3))
                buf.append(f'\x1b[38;2;{r};{g};{b}m{chr(0x2800 + random.randint(1, 255))}')
            buf.append('\x1b[0m\n')
        sys.stdout.write(''.join(buf)); sys.stdout.flush(); time.sleep(0.033)
finally:
    sys.stdout.write('\x1b[?1049l\x1b[?25h\x1b[0m')
```

## What we verified

- Reproduced twice today with the real animation (first with continuous 24-bit fades, then again after quantizing every emitted channel to 32 levels — quantization did **not** prevent it).
- `Developer: Reload Window` fully restores rendering every time.
- The emitting program writes only to its own tty (`/dev/tty`, alt screen, restores state on exit) — the cross-terminal effect is renderer-side.

## Possibly related

- #315782 (GPU texture cache residue under memory pressure) — similar residue symptom, different trigger (ours needs no lock/unlock or memory-pressure event, just sustained glyph-diverse output).
- #311614 (terminal rendering corrupted after macOS lock/unlock) — same "atlas gone bad until reload" family; ours is Linux/Remote-SSH and self-inflicted by output content.

Happy to run instrumented builds or provide more traces — reproduction is reliable on this setup.

title: Improve sandbox chat session discovery and handling of rate limits
body:
Sandbox chat sessions sometimes don't appear in the sessions list until you create a new sandbox session — at which point all of them show up at once.

### Root cause

Discovery is the only thing that surfaces sandbox sessions, and it was its own worst enemy. Each pass resolved **every** sandbox task with a single `Promise.all`, so a user with a few dozen tasks issued a few dozen simultaneous requests and tripped GitHub's rate limit.

From a user's log (~350 tasks, 38 of them sandbox tasks), 68 HTTP 429s in tight bursts:

```
8 at 17:22:58    2 at 17:22:59
8 at 17:24:54    2 at 17:24:56
9 at 18:12:36    1 at 18:12:38
```

Two failure modes follow:

1. **Sessions silently missing.** 8-9 `getTask` calls were rejected on every pass, so each "successful" pass was really `partial` and dropped roughly a quarter of the user's sessions. Nothing retried them.
2. **Nothing at all.** The burst starved whichever pass ran next. A window reloaded ~30s later had its `listTasks` page 1 fail, and page 1 failing returns `failed` — which seeds nothing and registers no providers. That window showed zero sandbox sessions.

Creating a new session appears to fix it because a failed pass leaves **zero** providers registered, and the new-chat composer calls `rediscover()` precisely when the host list is empty. By then the rate limit has recovered, so every session lands at once. Nothing else recovers: there is no timer, no backoff, and no refresh on focus.

### Changes

- **Bounded the fan-out.** Task-detail fetches now run through a `Limiter` capped at 5 concurrent instead of all at once. This is the root cause fix.
- **Retry rate-limited discovery reads.** A new `_retryWhileRateLimited` wraps `listTasks`, `getTask` and the repository-name lookup. It honors a server-supplied `Retry-After` **verbatim** and applies exponential backoff (1s → 2s → 4s, capped at 8s) only when the response names none.
- **Bounded the pass with a wait budget rather than a per-wait cap.** Shortening a server `Retry-After` would re-issue the request inside the window the server just asked us to stay out of — with `Retry-After: 60` that meant retries at 8s/16s/24s, three more 429s, and the session dropped anyway. A delay that doesn't fit the remaining budget now ends the retries instead, so the read reports its 429 and leaves the scan `partial` for a later pass.

Scoped to discovery only. Credential mints, task creation and history replay are untouched.

### Validation

- 5 new tests: peak concurrency stays at 5 across 30 tasks; a task that 429s twice still resolves; a rate-limited `listTasks` page 1 no longer fails the pass; a long `Retry-After` is not re-issued early; a persistently limited task gives up and leaves the scan `partial`.
- 112 passing across the sandbox and remote-agent-host provider suites.
- `typecheck-client` and eslint clean.

### Not covered

If discovery still fails for an unrelated reason (genuine network loss), the list stays empty until something triggers `rediscover()`. Retrying a failed pass in `CloudSandboxAgentHostContribution` would close that gap and is worth a follow-up.

title: Adopt SDK-managed AHP subscriptions and retire duplicate reconnect lifecycle
body:
## Context

VS Code currently owns both application-specific agent state projection and generic Agent Host Protocol subscription lifetime machinery.

The generic lifetime portion is split across:

- src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/agentSubscription.ts in AgentSubscriptionManager
- src/vs/platform/agentHost/browser/agentHostProtocolClient.ts in reconnect inventory and restoration

The official TypeScript SDK now has a proposed shared lifetime owner in microsoft/agent-host-protocol#423. A tested dependent slice on joshmouch/agent-host-protocol branch pr/typescript-managed-host-subscriptions preserves one logical lease across transport generations and owns replay/snapshot/missing restoration plus generation fencing.

## Proposed coordinated cutover

1. Land the SDK shared-subscription slice in microsoft/agent-host-protocol#423.
2. Land the dependent host-generation lease slice in the official SDK.
3. Migrate VS Code AHP consumers to acquire named managed leases from the SDK.
4. Feed restored snapshots and actions from those leases into the existing VS Code state projections and pending-action reconciler.
5. Delete the superseded generic lifecycle owner in VS Code:
   - currentSubscriptionUris reconnect inventory
   - generic holder/refcount/final-unsubscribe bookkeeping
   - generic subscription recreation after transport replacement
   - replay-versus-snapshot and missing-resource lifecycle routing
   - late-result and stale transport-generation fencing
   - the subscription-lifecycle portion of _applyReconnectResult, applyReconnectSnapshot, and markSubscriptionsMissing

## Ownership boundary after the cutover

The official AHP SDK owns protocol-generic subscription identity, holder lifetime, reconnect generation, restoration status, missing-resource state, and final unsubscribe.

VS Code continues to own application semantics: TypeScript reducers, value and verifiedValue projections, per-resource routing, optimistic write-ahead actions, own-action acknowledgement, pending-action persistence and resend, createSession gating, URI/Event/Disposable adaptation, logging, telemetry, authentication, tunnels, and UI integration.

This proposal does not claim that the VS Code TypeScript reducers are generated or Microsoft AHP SDK reducers. Any reducer extraction should be a separate proposal with its own compatibility and ownership review. The handwritten C# reducers in the .NET AHP client were authored by Joshua Mouch and are also a separate provenance concern.

## Acceptance

- One logical subscription object survives a real transport replacement.
- Replay restoration, snapshot restoration, and missing-resource restoration use that same object.
- Events and late results from abandoned generations are ignored.
- Initial and managed owners may share a URI without duplicate subscribe or premature unsubscribe.
- Last-holder release sends exactly one unsubscribe through the current generation.
- Existing VS Code optimistic and confirmed state behavior remains green.
- Deleted VS Code code has no remaining caller or compatibility wrapper.

Related: microsoft/agent-host-protocol#423 and microsoft/agent-host-protocol#422.

title: Let a host declare which changeset the Changes view defaults to
body:
## The problem

On a cloud sandbox session the Changes panel says **No Changed Files** while the chat reports `1 file changed +2 −0`. Both are telling the truth — they answer different questions.

The panel defaulted to **Branch Changes** (`changeKind: 'branch'`), which means *the commits `HEAD` introduces relative to its merge-base with the base branch*. A sandbox agent edits files in the working tree without committing, so `branch` is legitimately empty.

The default was hardcoded:

```ts
const defaultChangeset = changesets.find(c => c.changeKind === ChangesetKind.Branch) ?? changesets[0];
```

That is a sensible default for a host whose agent commits as it goes. It is the wrong one for a sandbox.

## The change

Rather than teach the generic changeset code about sandboxes, let a host declare what it wants. `IAgentHostAdapterOptions` gains an optional `defaultChangesetKind`, threaded through the existing provider-config path already used for per-host traits like `sessionSchemeAlias` and `workspaceTypeIcon`:

```ts
// cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.ts
sessionSchemeAlias: SANDBOX_SESSION_SCHEME_ALIAS,
// The sandbox agent edits without committing, so `branch` is always empty.
defaultChangesetKind: ChangesetKind.Session,
```

The selection keeps its original shape — only the kind being looked up becomes configurable:

```ts
const defaultKind = options.defaultChangesetKind ?? ChangesetKind.Branch;
const defaultChangeset = changesets.find(c => c.changeKind === defaultKind) ?? changesets[0];
```

A host that declares nothing — every local session, and every remote host that is not a sandbox — resolves `defaultKind` to `branch` and behaves exactly as before.

## Why `session` for a sandbox

`session` is the changeset whose entry reads *"Cumulative file edits the agent has made in this session."* It is derived from the agent's own tool calls rather than from git, so it shows the agent's work whether or not anything was committed — which is what someone opening the Changes panel on a sandbox session is asking to see.

The other candidate was `all` (working tree vs. the base-branch merge-base, the union of `branch` and `uncommitted`). It would also have fixed the empty panel, but it is a git query rather than a record of the agent's work, and it is labelled "All Changes" — colliding with the label this host already uses for its own `session` changeset. Preferring `session` avoids introducing that ambiguity.

## Alternatives considered

- **Fall back when the selected changeset is empty.** "Empty" and "still loading" are indistinguishable at selection time, so the panel would flicker between views as diffs arrive.
- **Detect the sandbox inside `createChangesets`** by comparing the session URI scheme against `CLOUD_SANDBOX_SESSION_SCHEME`. Works, but puts knowledge of one specific host inside generic code. Declaring the preference at the host keeps the dependency pointing the right way.
- **Use whichever entry the host lists first.** Both hosts happen to lead their catalogue with the view they consider primary, so this would produce the right answer today with no new option — but nothing in the protocol promises that ordering, and the rule would silently change behaviour for every host if a catalogue were ever reordered.

## Tests

Six cases in `agentHostSessionChangesets.test.ts` covering the declared preference, the untouched fallback, and a preference the catalogue does not advertise.

Each was control-tested — the production change was reverted piecewise and the failure reason checked, not just the failure:

| Reverted | Fails | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| The declared preference is ignored (`defaultKind` pinned to `branch`) | the declared-preference test, and the not-advertised test | `branch*` instead of `session*` |
| The fallback kind is wrong (`?? ChangesetKind.Session`) | both no-preference tests | `session*` where `branch*` was expected |

The two no-preference tests pass with and without the fix by design: they are regression guards pinning that hosts which declare nothing are unaffected, and they are what catches an over-broad implementation.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — clean
- `npx eslint` on the five changed files — clean
- `./scripts/test.sh --glob "**/vs/{sessions,workbench/contrib/chat,platform/agentHost}/**/*.test.js"` — 14781 passing, 0 failing

Not verified end to end against a live sandbox session; that needs a human.

title: agentHost: gate turns through an onIncomingRequest chat contribution hook
body:
agentHost: gate turns through an onIncomingRequest chat contribution hook

Adds an admission hook to the chat contribution model and moves the read-only guard and
local command interception onto it. Turn admission was duplicated: `handleAction` and
`QueueDrainContribution` each ran the same preamble, and the read-only guard sat further
down in the send path. Admission now has one route and one copy.

- Adds `onIncomingRequest`, which decides whether a turn may proceed to its provider. A
  contribution returns `accept`, `handled`, or `reject`, and the first non-accept
  disposition wins.
- Makes the hook fail closed. Every other hook skips a contribution that throws; a throwing
  admission contribution rejects the request instead. The gate stops a client from running
  work in a session that can have no worktree on disk, so a failure must not open it.
- Makes the hook synchronous. A gate must decide before the send path awaits, so the state
  it reads cannot change before the decision takes effect. An asynchronous version deferred
  the read-only guard by one microtask and broke three existing tests.
- Adds `TurnAdmissionContribution` (order 100), which rejects turns on read-only chats and
  archived sessions.
- Adds `LocalCommandContribution` (order 50), which handles `/rename` and `!command`. The
  order is load-bearing: local commands were always intercepted before the read-only guard,
  so they stay available in read-only and archived chats.
- Adds the `startTurn` function, which runs the shared preamble: the gate, title seeding,
  provider lookup, the `noAgent` error, and turn telemetry. Both admission paths invoke it
  with `IInstantiationService.invokeFunction`. It is a function and not a service because it
  holds no state, so a service registration would only add one line to every hand-built test
  service graph.
- Moves `AgentHostTurnFailureStage` to `common` so the disposition can name a failure stage.
  The node telemetry reporter re-exports it, so no importer changes.
- Removes the admission block from `_sendTurnMessage`, which is now only the send tail.
- Accepts that a rejected turn no longer reports `userMessageSent` or `turnCompleted`. The
  gate runs before `turnStarted`, so there is no turn to complete. `chatContributions/TODO.md`
  records this.
- Rewrites `chatContributions/TODO.md`. It listed `githubReferences` as an outgoing-turn
  contribution although it only implements `onTurnEnd`, and described an admission flow that
  no longer exists. Adds a table of all six hooks and their contributions in order.

title: VS Code renderer causes severe memory/commit leak while idle, eventually freezing Windows
body:
# VS Code renderer causes severe memory/commit leak while idle, eventually freezing Windows

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested yet

* VS Code Version: 1.135.0
* Commit: 08d4889f9ec4a1685d257b9b95de036c8e1ce1e5
* Architecture: x64
* OS Version: Windows 10.0.26200.9168
* Physical RAM: approximately 32 GB

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start VS Code with my normal development environment.
2. The environment includes WSL, Docker Desktop, Node.js/Next.js server and worker processes.
3. Leave the development environment running while the machine is mostly idle.
4. After some time, system committed memory starts increasing rapidly.
5. Commit usage eventually reaches approximately 98–100%.
6. Windows becomes almost completely unresponsive. At that point I cannot reliably open Task Manager or execute diagnostic commands.
7. A hardware reset/reboot is required.

## Actual Behavior

VS Code appears to cause a severe memory/resource leak while the machine is mostly idle.

During one captured occurrence, system committed memory increased from approximately:

`18.2 GB`

to approximately:

`36.2 GB`

in about 11 minutes.

The commit limit at the time was approximately:

`36.9 GB`

so commit usage reached approximately:

`97.9%`

Once this happened, Windows became effectively unusable.

## Suspicious VS Code Process

The primary suspect is a VS Code `Code.exe` renderer process.

Immediately before the system became unusable, this renderer process showed approximately:

* PID: `14700`
* Working Set: `~2.16 GB`
* Private / committed memory: `~2.45 GB`
* Handle count: `~122,745`

The handle count appears extremely abnormal.

For comparison, another main VS Code process had only approximately:

`~1,150 handles`

Total committed memory for all VS Code processes at the time of the snapshot was approximately:

`~4.65 GB`

The unusually high handle count in this renderer process is the most suspicious observation from the captured diagnostics.

## Node.js Processes

Node.js processes were also using a significant amount of committed memory.

One Next.js process running `start-server.js` showed approximately:

* Working Set: `~1.92 GB`
* Committed memory: `~3.67 GB`

Total committed memory for all Node.js processes at that time was approximately:

`~5.18 GB`

It is possible that the issue involves an interaction between VS Code, the renderer, file watchers, extensions, Node.js/Next.js, or the development worker.

## WSL / Docker Observations

WSL and Docker do not appear to be the primary source of the memory growth.

At approximately the same time:

* `vmmemWSL`: `~1.52 GB`
* Actual used memory inside WSL: `~582 MB`
* Redis Docker container: `~14 MB`

The system-wide increase in committed memory therefore does not appear to correspond to memory usage inside WSL or Docker containers.

## Important Reproduction Detail

There is one unusual behavior that may be relevant.

I initially used a diagnostic PowerShell script that periodically queried:

* WSL memory
* Docker statistics
* Windows performance information

When this diagnostic script was running continuously, the memory leak often did not reproduce.

When the machine was left genuinely idle without those periodic WSL/Docker queries, the memory growth occurred again.

This suggests that the issue may depend on an idle state, timing, renderer behavior, file watching, background cleanup, or another process state that is changed when WSL/Docker are periodically queried.

In other words, periodically waking/querying the development environment appears to influence whether the problem reproduces.

## Impact

This is not only increased memory usage.

The end result is a complete system-level failure:

1. VS Code and the development environment are left running.
2. The machine becomes mostly idle.
3. Committed memory starts increasing rapidly.
4. Commit usage approaches 100%.
5. Windows becomes too unresponsive to terminate VS Code or collect further diagnostics.
6. The computer has to be physically reset/rebooted.

## Additional Testing

I am currently testing:

* VS Code with GPU hardware acceleration disabled
* VS Code with extensions disabled
* different combinations of the Node.js/Next.js server and worker processes
* a larger Windows page file so that the system remains responsive long enough to collect more diagnostics

I have a larger diagnostic archive from the affected system, but I am not attaching it publicly because it contains machine/user metadata.

If useful, I can provide specific sanitized logs, process information, handle data, performance traces, renderer dumps, or other targeted diagnostics requested by the VS Code team.

4. Call `createSession` with a new client-chosen `ahp-session:/<uuid>`, provider `copilotcli`, working directory, valid config, and an `activeClient` matching the initializing client ID.
5. Subscribe to the exact session resource.
6. Wait for `session/ready` or `session/creationFailed`.

## Actual

The session snapshot remains:

```text
lifecycle: creating
```

It already contains:

- a valid server-generated `defaultChat`
- the same chat in `SessionState.chats`

But no `session/ready` or `session/creationFailed` arrives. The only session actions observed during the wait are `session/metaChanged`.

This remained unchanged with and without `activeClient`.

If the client violates the normative ordering and sends a neutral first turn to the advertised default chat anyway:

1. the chat turn completes;
2. a fresh session snapshot then reports `lifecycle: ready`.

## Expected

Per the AHP 1.0 session lifecycle, the host should emit `session/ready` after backend initialization, before the client needs to start a turn.

Clients should not need to send a first turn to make the session become ready, because the documented flow requires waiting for readiness before using the session.

## Impact

Strict AHP 1.0 clients deadlock:

- the host waits for a first turn to materialize the backend;
- the client waits for `session/ready` before sending that turn.

The only workaround is a VS Code-specific bounded exception: when lifecycle is still `creating` but a valid default chat is already catalogued, send a neutral materializing turn and then require a fresh session snapshot to become `ready`.

## Related, but not duplicate

- #331118 covers a first-turn customization refresh that leaves an active turn permanently stuck.

This report is about the earlier session-lifecycle transition: no turn has been sent yet, and `session/ready` is withheld until one is sent.

title: AHP listSessions fails globally when Claude provider catalog is unavailable

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: N/A (built-in Agent Host)
- VS Code Version: 1.135.0 (`08d4889f9ec4a1685d257b9b95de036c8e1ce1e5`)
- OS Version: Linux remote container; macOS client
- Feature: Agent Host Protocol 1.0 `listSessions`
- Selected model: GPT-5.6 Sol
- Logs: Redacted error and source-level analysis included below

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a standalone VS Code Agent Host using fresh isolated `--user-data-dir` and `--server-data-dir` directories.
2. Connect over the token-protected loopback WebSocket.
3. Send an AHP 1.0 `initialize` request with `initialSubscriptions: ["ahp-root://"]`.
4. Authenticate every advertised protected resource.
5. Confirm Copilot models are advertised and `ping` succeeds.
6. Call:

   ```json
   {
     "jsonrpc": "2.0",
     "id": 2,
     "method": "listSessions",
     "params": {
       "channel": "ahp-root://",
       "limit": 2
     }
   }
   ```

## Actual

The entire command fails:

```text
-32603 ProviderCatalogUnavailableError:
Provider claude cannot enumerate its native session catalog yet
```

Waiting and retrying does not repair it. The same failure occurs with both a persistent profile and a completely fresh isolated profile.

Meanwhile, all of the following continue to work:

- AHP 1.0 `initialize`
- `ping`
- protected-resource authentication
- Copilot model discovery
- `resolveSessionConfig`
- direct `createSession`
- direct session/chat subscriptions
- chat turns and completion
- reconnect replay
- session disposal

## Expected

One unavailable provider-native external catalogue should not fail the entire Agent Host session catalogue.

Any of these would be preferable:

1. Return locally registered sessions while omitting the unavailable provider's external sessions.
2. Return a partial result with provider-level diagnostics.
3. Mark Claude catalogue discovery unavailable and retry it independently.

## Source-level cause

In `AgentService._migrateLegacyProviderChats`, an undefined provider catalogue throws `ProviderCatalogUnavailableError`. `listSessions()` awaits initial provider migration before listing the Agent Host registry, so one provider blocks every registered session.

## Related, but not duplicate

- #329619 covers ignored `limit`/`cursor` pagination.
- #331155 covers slow Copilot catalogue migration.

This issue is specifically about one unavailable provider failing the whole `listSessions` command, including locally registered sessions from other healthy providers.

title: chat: choose compatibility when creating Agent Plugins
body:
## Summary

- generate a canonical Agent Plugins 1.0 package from **Chat: Create Plugin**
- after resource selection, offer either the standard package or the standard package with additive legacy compatibility files
- keep portable and Copilot-specific components in their sanctioned Agent Plugins locations
- validate MCP definitions before writing files and preserve SSE/Streamable HTTP semantics without exporting configured headers

Fixes #332811

## Format choices

- **Agent Plugin** — Standard plugin format
- **Open Plugin (Legacy Compatibility)** — Also supports older clients

Both choices generate the same valid Agent Plugins 1.0 package. Compatibility mode additionally projects the selected resources into `.plugin/plugin.json`, legacy `commands/`, `agents/`, `rules/`, `hooks/hooks.json`, and `.mcp.json` paths. The canonical root manifest and component paths remain authoritative and cause modern clients to detect the package as an Agent Plugin.

## Decision log

- **Agent Plugins 1.0 is always canonical.** Generated content should be as future-proof and portable as possible.
- **Compatibility is additive, not an alternate legacy-only package.** Older clients get redundant legacy paths without weakening or omitting the standard representation.
- **The choice follows resource selection.** Users first choose what to package, then decide whether older-client compatibility files are needed.
- **Use established compatibility terminology.** The picker labels the additive compatibility choice `Open Plugin (Legacy Compatibility)` while the canonical package remains Agent Plugins 1.0.
- **Canonical validity gates both modes.** If an MCP server cannot be represented safely by Agent Plugins 1.0, creation fails before writing files rather than producing a legacy-only partial package.
- **Credential safety applies to both modes.** Configured HTTP headers are never copied into distributable output.
- **Internal parser naming is unchanged.** Existing `PluginFormat.OpenPlugin` terminology remains an implementation detail outside this PR’s scope.

### What it generates

`writePluginToDisk` in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/actions/createPluginAction.ts` writes:

```text
my-plugin/
├── .plugin/
│   └── plugin.json       # { name, version, description } — no $schema
├── rules/
├── commands/
├── agents/
├── skills/
├── hooks/
│   └── hooks.json
└── .mcp.json
```

`detectPluginFormat` in `src/vs/platform/agentPlugins/common/pluginParsers.ts` resolves this to `PluginFormat.OpenPlugin`, since the manifest is at `.plugin/plugin.json` with no `$schema`, rather than `PluginFormat.AgentPlugin`.

### Path comparison

| Component | Agent Plugins 1.0 | Generated |
|---|---|---|
| manifest | `plugin.json` (root, with `$schema`) | `.plugin/plugin.json` |
| skills | `skills/` | `skills/` ✅ |
| MCP servers | `mcp.json` | `.mcp.json` |
| agents | `com.github.copilot/agents/` | `agents/` |
| commands | `com.github.copilot/commands/` | `commands/` |
| rules | `com.github.copilot/rules/` | `rules/` |
| hooks | `com.github.copilot/hooks/hooks.json` | `hooks/hooks.json` |

Only `skills/` matches. Plugins created through this action aren't portable to other Agent Plugins clients and aren't a valid starting point for the `com.github.copilot` namespace, since four component directories sit at the wrong location.

### Fix

Generate an Agent Plugins 1.0 package:

```text
my-plugin/
├── plugin.json               # { $schema, name, version, description }
├── skills/
├── mcp.json
└── com.github.copilot/
    ├── agents/
    ├── commands/
    ├── rules/
    └── hooks/
        └── hooks.json
```

The manifest schema is closed (`$schema`, `name`, `version`, `description`, `author`, `homepage`, `repository`, `license`, `keywords`, `extensions` only), so no component path fields should be emitted. Confirm `validatePluginName` against the spec's name constraints (periods allowed, no `--` or `..`).

Tests in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/actions/createPluginAction.test.ts` assert the current paths and need updating alongside.

### References

* Spec: https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/blob/main/spec/1.0.0.md
* Client extension directories (§8.2): https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec/blob/main/spec/1.0.0.md#82-extension-directories
* VS Code namespace support: #329473

### Summary
Changing the chat mode picker (Agent → Ask/Plan) while an unsent draft is in the
input box discards the draft and automatically resubmits the previous request.
In my session this repeatedly resubmitted `Start implementation`, which executed
in Agent mode and modified files without my intent.

1. Open Copilot Chat in Agent mode.
2. Send a request and let it complete.

not a submit action.

- The previous request is resubmitted automatically.

This happened 4 times in a single session. Because the resubmitted request ran in
Agent mode, the agent performed substantial unrequested work: created and edited

title: nes: apply supportsUnifiedCompletions on the default provider path
body:
## Summary

Follow-up hotfix to #332018. The `supportsUnifiedCompletions` capability (baked into the `patchBased02Optimized` prompting strategy) was only wired into the **joint** completions provider (`JointCompletionsProviderContribution`), which is gated behind `chat.advanced.inlineEdits.jointCompletionsProvider.enabled` (default **`false`**).

On the **default** provider path, `InlineEditProviderFeature.registerProvider()` registers NES and suppresses the separate completions/ghost-text provider via a `modelUnification`-derived `excludes` list. Because that block only consulted the core `unificationStateValue?.modelUnification`, a model that sets `supportsUnifiedCompletions` purely through its prompting strategy (e.g. a `copilot-proxy` `/models` deployment with no ExP/local unification toggles) still emitted ghost-text completions.

## Fix

Derive the effective unification in `InlineEditProviderFeature` from the baked `supportsUnifiedCompletions` flag, OR-ed with the core `modelUnification` state, and use it to gate the `excludes`:

```ts
const modelUnification = this._supportsUnifiedCompletions.read(reader) || (unificationStateValue?.modelUnification ?? false);
```

When set, both `'completions'` and `'github.copilot'` are excluded -- matching the `excludedProviders: "completions,github.copilot"` behavior the strategy is meant to replace. The flag is observed reactively via `IInlineEditsModelService.onModelListUpdated`, mirroring the wiring already added to the joint provider in #332018. The core experiment/deployment path is unchanged for models that do not set the flag.

## Known limitations

- **Startup flicker (fetched `/models` path only).** `supportsUnifiedCompletions` is the only strategy-baked value read at provider-registration time rather than per-request, so it depends on the async `/models` resolution. During the cold-start window before the fetch resolves, `selectedModelConfiguration()` has no strategy yet, the flag reads `false`, and the separate completions provider is not yet excluded -- so ghost text can briefly appear. It self-corrects the instant `onModelListUpdated` fires (the observable has no debounce and re-registers immediately). This does **not** affect local/ExP model configuration, which resolves synchronously at startup. Fully eliminating the window would require holding the separate `github.copilot` completions provider until the NES model list first resolves; that is a larger change tracked in #332837 and intentionally left out of this hotfix.
- **`forceUseDefaultModel` fallback drops baked knobs (pre-existing, all strategies).** If the deployed model returns `NotFound` (404), the provider falls back to `defaultModelConfiguration()`, which does not apply `applyStrategyConfig`. All strategy-baked values are bypassed under this fallback -- this is shared graceful-degradation behavior affecting every strategy (including `patchBased02WithRecentLineNumbers`), not specific to `patchBased02Optimized`.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck --prefix extensions/copilot` (changed file clean)
- focused Vitest for `applyStrategyConfig` / `MODEL_CONFIGURATION_VALIDATOR` and `UserInteractionMonitor`
- `npm run precommit`

title: sessions: Show pending approvals on their own chat rows
body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #332739 (nested chats shown as child rows under each session). Now that a session's nested chats render as their own rows, this surfaces each chat's pending tool approval **on that chat's row** instead of aggregating every chat's approval onto the parent session row.

## What changed

- **Per-chat approval rows**: `SessionChatItemRenderer` now renders a chat's pending approval (command label + **Allow** button) on the chat's own row, keyed on that chat's resource. The row layout became a flex column: a fixed-height title row with the approval stacked beneath it.
- **Session row shows only its main chat's approval**: the parent session row uses `getMainChatApproval` (main chat only) instead of aggregating across all chats. Nested/side chats surface their approvals on their own rows.
- **Flat, chat-less lists unchanged**: the blocked-sessions dropdown and automations view render no nested chat rows, so their session rows still aggregate an approval from *any* of a session's chats. This is gated by a new `aggregateChatApprovals` flag on the shared renderer/delegate.
- **Shared rendering**: the approval-row markup + "Allow" behavior are extracted into a shared `renderApprovalRowContent` helper, and the CSS is hoisted to a top-level `.session-approval-row` rule so the session row and chat rows render identically.
- **Virtualization**: the tree delegate reserves the extra row height for a chat with a pending approval (plus a small bottom slack for code-block line-height rounding) and updates it reactively via `onDidChangeItemHeight` as approvals appear and clear.

## Why

With multiple chats per session, aggregating all approvals onto the parent row made it ambiguous which chat needed input and only surfaced one approval at a time. Rendering each approval on its owning chat row makes the pending action unambiguous and lets multiple sibling chats show their approvals simultaneously.

## Notes for reviewers

- Behavior preserved for: the main chat represented by the parent session row, nested/ordinary/side chats, the Allow action, accessibility labels, virtualization/disposal, phone layout, and the flat blocked-sessions/automations lists.
- `mainChat.resource` is guarded so a session with an unresolved main chat simply shows no approval.

## Testing
